questions.question: What was Mansa Musa's title 'Mansa' mean?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'Mansa', meaning 'ruler' or 'king' in MandÃ©, was the title of the ruler of the Mali Empire.
Incorrect. 'Hajji' is the title given to someone who has made the hajj, not 'Mansa'.
Incorrect. The article does not say that 'Mansa' means gold trader.
Incorrect. The article does not say that 'Mansa' means general.

questions.question: What was the main source of Mansa Musa's wealth?
options: Control and taxing of trade in salt and gold
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says his wealth came principally from the Mali Empire's control and taxing of the trade in salt from northern regions and especially from gold panned and mined in Bambuk and Bure.
Incorrect. The article mentions spices as one of many goods traded, but not as the main source of his wealth.
Incorrect. The article does not say he rented out his army.
Incorrect. The article does not mention farming as a source of his wealth.

questions.question: When did Mansa Musa go on the Hajj to Mecca?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that Musa went on Hajj to Mecca in 1324.
Incorrect. 1310 is not mentioned as the year of his hajj.
Incorrect. 1337 is given as the approximate end of his reign, not the year of his hajj.
Incorrect. 1300 is not mentioned as the year of his hajj.

questions.question: Which cities did Mansa Musa incorporate into the Mali Empire?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says that Musa expanded the borders of the Mali Empire, in particular incorporating the cities of Gao and Timbuktu into its territory.
Incorrect. Cairo and Mecca were cities he visited during his hajj, not incorporated into Mali.
Incorrect. Medina and Suez were on his pilgrimage route, not incorporated into Mali.
Incorrect. Bambuk and Bure were gold-producing regions, not cities he incorporated.

questions.question: What happened to Mansa Musa's predecessor according to Musa's own account?
options: He led an expedition to explore the Atlantic Ocean and did not return
He was killed in a battle
He retired and became a religious leader
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says that according to Musa's own account, his predecessor launched expeditions to explore the Atlantic Ocean, led the second expedition himself, and when he did not return, Musa was crowned as mansa.
Incorrect. The article does not say he was killed in battle.
Incorrect. The article does not say he died of illness.
Incorrect. The article does not say he retired.

questions.question: Who did Mansa Musa meet while in Cairo during his hajj?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says that while in Cairo, Musa met with the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad.
Incorrect. Musa met al-Sahili on his return journey, not in Cairo.
Incorrect. Ibn Khaldun wrote about Musa but is not mentioned as meeting him in Cairo.
Incorrect. Ibn Battuta visited Mali during the reign of Musa's brother Sulayman, not during Musa's reign.

questions.question: What did Mansa Musa do with gold during his journey to Mecca?
options: He distributed gold to the poor and to cities along the route
He kept all the gold for himself
He buried the gold in the desert
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says that Musa is said to have distributed gold to the poor along his route and to the cities he passed through on the way to Mecca.
Incorrect. The article explicitly says he gave gold away.
Incorrect. The article does not mention trading gold for horses.
Incorrect. The article does not mention burying gold.

questions.question: What did Mansa Musa do after his return from Mecca?
options: He brought scholars and architects to Mali and helped establish Timbuktu as a center of Islamic learning
He went on another pilgrimage to Jerusalem
He conquered all of North Africa
He gave up his throne and became a hermit
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says he recruited scholars from the wider Muslim world to travel to Mali and helped establish Timbuktu as a center of Islamic learning, and he also brought architects to build his palace and the Djinguereber Mosque.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a pilgrimage to Jerusalem.
Incorrect. The article does not say he conquered North Africa.
Incorrect. The article does not say he gave up his throne.

questions.question: According to the article, what did Mansa Musa's entourage include on his hajj?
options: Thousands of slaves and camels carrying gold
A group of musicians and dancers
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says his procession included upwards of 12,000 slaves, each carrying gold bars, and 80 camels carrying gold dust.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a large army of soldiers in his entourage.
Incorrect. The article does not mention elephants.
Incorrect. The article does not mention musicians and dancers.

questions.question: What happened to Mansa Musa's entourage on the return journey from Mecca?
options: Many died of cold, starvation, or bandit raids, and they lost much of their supplies
They were captured and sold as slaves
They were welcomed by every city and given many gifts
They found a faster route and returned quickly
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says that by the time they reached Suez, many of the Malian pilgrims had died of cold, starvation, or bandit raids, and they had lost much of their supplies.
Incorrect. The article does not say they were captured and sold as slaves.
Incorrect. The article says they suffered hardships, not that they were welcomed with gifts.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a faster route.
